title: Corner Set Construction
content: Defines cornerSet A as the set of pairs (x,y) in (Z/NZ)^2 where 2x+y lies in A. The simp lemma provides direct membership access.
mathContext: The coefficient 2 in '2x+y' is crucial: it's the unique coefficient c such that corners in {(x,y) : cx+y in A} correspond to 3-term arithmetic progressions in A.

title: Corners to 3-APs
content: If (x,y), (x+d,y), (x,y+d) are all in cornerSet A with d nonzero, then {2x+y, 2x+y+d, 2x+y+2d} is a 3-AP in A. Proved by ring arithmetic.
mathContext: The three membership conditions give: 2x+y in A, 2(x+d)+y = 2x+y+2d in A, 2x+(y+d) = 2x+y+d in A. The ring tactic verifies the equalities.

title: 3-APs to Corners
content: Each 3-AP {a, a+d, a+2d} in A produces a corner in S for every x in Z/NZ (with y = a-2x). This gives N corners per 3-AP.
mathContext: The parameterization by x reveals the N-fold multiplicity: each AP element maps to an entire fiber of corners, amplifying the structure.

title: AP-Free Implies Corner-Free
content: If A has no 3-term AP, then cornerSet A has no corners. This is the contrapositive reduction from the corners theorem to Roth's theorem.
mathContext: This is the key logical step: it converts the additive combinatorics problem (no 3-AP) into a geometric problem (no corner in Z/NZ x Z/NZ), which the regularity method can solve.
